description: Use this when the user asks to learn, study, memorize, review, practice, or create flashcards about any topic. Generate the complete deck in this call and open it in the interactive flashcard UI. Act immediately using the existing conversation and source material; infer language and backLanguage yourself. Never ask the user for language codes, tool arguments, or confirmation of an already requested deck. For a request for 50 cards, submit all 50 completed cards in one call. Keep the response brief and let the study UI show the deck. Examples include 'I want to learn about X', 'teach me X with flashcards', and 'Create an HSK3 vocabulary deck about restaurants'. Do not call a separate add-card tool. Do NOT use when the user asks for a direct explanation without study intent, asks to delete or modify an existing deck, or requests an in-conversation quiz without creating a deck.

backLanguage.description: Language of the translations on the back. Set from the user’s known language; never assume English. Always set for language-learning decks. Used for reverse-card audio.

cards.description: The complete generated deck. Include exactly the number of cards the user requested, with every required language-learning field completed; never submit a partial array or placeholders.

back.description: Answer, definition, translation, or explanation. For language learning, always use the user's known language (e.g. English). This is the revealed answer when the card is flipped.

example.description: A concise example sentence or usage phrase in the target or subject language. Include when the user requests examples or when teaching a language.

exampleParts.description: For Chinese examples only: every part of the example in order, split into useful words or short semantic phrases. Encode each part compactly as [Chinese text, tone-marked pinyin, direct translation]. Cover the complete example exactly once in no more than 12 parts; attach punctuation to the preceding part.

items.description: Exactly three strings in this order: [Chinese word or short semantic phrase, tone-marked pinyin for that segment, direct translation of that segment]. Attach adjacent punctuation to the Chinese text.

examplePronunciation.description: Pronunciation or romanization of the example sentence.

exampleTranslation.description: Translation or plain-language explanation of the example.

front.description: Prompt, question, term, word, or phrase. For language learning, always use the target language (the language being learned). For example: Chinese characters, Italian phrases, or Japanese words.

pronunciation.description: Pinyin, romaji, IPA, or another reading guide for the front text. Required for language decks with non-Latin script (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, etc.) and when the user requests pronunciation.

language.description: ISO 639-1 code for the language spoken on the front side (e.g. 'zh' Chinese, 'ja' Japanese, 'vi' Vietnamese). Used for the correct audio voice and saved-deck language. Always infer and set it from the user's target language, never from their current app preference.

title.description: A concise, descriptive title for the generated deck.
